editor.title: Script Editor
editor.objects: Insertable objects (double-click to insert; right-click props / variables for read or write code)

scriptHelp.title: Script Help
scriptHelp.editorText:
Toolbar, left to right: Save Ctrl+S (writes back to the original dialog draft; you still need to confirm there to persist), Cut Ctrl+X, Copy Ctrl+C, Paste Ctrl+V, Undo Ctrl+Z, Redo Ctrl+Y, Indent Ctrl+I (shift selected lines right), Outdent Ctrl+B, Comment Ctrl+' (toggle line comments), Check Ctrl+E (syntax check, errors shown at the bottom and as a message).
Quick insert: statement blocks (if-else, while, for, try-catch, return...), operators, brackets (wraps the selection), comment (wraps the selection in a block comment).
Top right is Find / Replace: type and click Find Next (Ctrl+F focuses find, Ctrl+R focuses replace), whole-word match supported, total count shown live; Replace replaces the current match then jumps to the next, Replace All replaces everything at once.
Bottom right is the insertable object tree: double-click any leaf to insert the code at the cursor (script API, widgets on the canvas with their props, internal variables).
Others: Select All Ctrl+A, Delete selection Ctrl+D, Help Ctrl+H; undo / redo / clipboard use the native editor capabilities.
scriptHelp.variablesText:
Internal variables belong to the data source "local". Their definitions are saved in the layout: add, rename or delete them in the variable manager (the Variables button in the editor toolbar, or the edit-mode toolbar), up to 200.
Variable values are runtime data and are not saved with the layout. Use scada.read / scada.write in global scripts, ctx.get in transform functions (auto-subscribes); widgets can also bind internal variables as data items.
Keys look like var17, auto-numbered and never reused after deletion; names are free-form, and both key and name work in scripts and bindings.

tool.undoDesc: Undo the last change, up to the last {max} steps ({n} available).
tool.redoDesc: Restore the change you just undid ({n} available).
tool.referenceHint: Reference object = the first widget you selected (orange frame). Align / same size use it as the standard and never move it. To change it, click it first when selecting, or click its flag in the Layers panel
tool.lockedHint: The selected widgets are locked; unlock them first
tool.alignLeftDesc: Align the selected objects with the left edge of the reference object.
tool.alignRightDesc: Align the selected objects with the right edge of the reference object.
tool.alignTopDesc: Align the selected objects with the top edge of the reference object.
tool.alignBottomDesc: Align the selected objects with the bottom edge of the reference object.
tool.alignCenterXDesc: Align the selected objects with the vertical center axis of the reference object (same center x).
tool.alignCenterYDesc: Align the selected objects with the horizontal center axis of the reference object (same center y).
tool.alignCenterDesc: Align the selected objects with the center point of the reference object.
tool.pageCenterXDesc: Put the geometric center of each selected object on the horizontal center line of the whole screen (left-right centered); each object keeps its vertical position.
tool.pageCenterYDesc: Put the geometric center of each selected object on the vertical center line of the whole screen (top-bottom centered); each object keeps its horizontal position.
tool.pageCenterDesc: Put the geometric center of each selected object on the center point of the whole screen.
tool.distributeDesc: Select at least 3 widgets: the two outermost stay put and the rest are spread evenly between them. The small triangle switches between 'equal gaps' and 'equal center distances'.
tool.sameWidthDesc: Make the selected objects as wide as the reference object.
tool.sameHeightDesc: Make the selected objects as tall as the reference object.
tool.sameSizeDesc: Make the selected objects the same width and height as the reference object.
tool.rotateCwDesc: Rotate the whole selection 90° clockwise (a single widget rotates around its own center).
tool.rotateCcwDesc: Rotate the whole selection 90° counterclockwise (a single widget rotates around its own center).
tool.flipHDesc: Mirror the whole selection left to right.
tool.flipVDesc: Mirror the whole selection top to bottom.
tool.groupDesc: Group the selected widgets: clicking one selects the whole group, and they move and resize together (Ctrl + G).
tool.ungroupDesc: Break up the group of the selected widgets (Ctrl + Shift + G).
tool.lockDesc: A locked widget cannot be dragged, resized, aligned, rotated, flipped or deleted (it can still be selected, edited and reordered).
tool.toFrontDesc: Move the selected widgets to the very top.
tool.toBackDesc: Move the selected widgets to the very bottom.
tool.forwardDesc: Move the selected widgets up one layer.
tool.backwardDesc: Move the selected widgets down one layer.
tool.gridDesc: Show and snap to the grid (on / off; the step is set in the canvas properties).

vars.hint:
Names appear in the 'Data Item' dropdown of a widget's properties (empty = the default 'Variable N').
The ID is numbered automatically, never reused and cannot be changed. Changes apply when you press OK and can be undone with Ctrl + Z.
Values are runtime data and are not exported with the layout; when a variable is deleted, its value is cleared when you save and leave edit mode.

help.title: How to use
help.paletteText:
Tap a widget: placed at the center of the current view (also after zooming / panning; repeated taps are staggered)
Press and drag onto the canvas: placed where you release
Click a category header to collapse it; switch grid / list view at the top right
help.canvasText:
Wheel / pinch: zoom around the pointer
Hold Space and drag, or drag with the middle mouse button: pan
Keys + / - / 0: zoom in / out / reset; the toolbar － 100% ＋ works too
help.widgetText:
Drag to move; drag the 8 handles on the selection frame to resize in any direction (Shift + corner: keep the aspect ratio)
Ctrl (⌘ on Mac) or Shift + click: add / remove from the selection; Ctrl + A selects all; clicking a grouped widget selects the whole group (Alt + click: just one)
Arrow keys nudge 1px, Shift + arrows step by the grid
Delete removes the selection; the property panel accepts exact position / size
Click a section title in the properties panel to collapse / expand it (your choice is remembered); rotate / flip are in the second toolbar row
Drag on an empty area (the canvas or the gray area around it) to box-select every widget fully inside the box (a group must be fully inside); hold Ctrl / Shift while dragging to add to the current selection
help.arrangeText:
Second toolbar row: align / distribute / same size / rotate / flip / group / lock / order / grid; align and same size use the 'reference object' (the first widget selected, orange frame) as the standard
Layers panel on the left: top to bottom = upper to lower layer on the canvas; click to select (Ctrl / Shift for several), drag the ⋮⋮ handle or use the buttons above to reorder, the eye / padlock hide / lock
Fullscreen button: the editor temporarily fills the whole screen (leave with Esc, by clicking again, or by saving / cancelling the edit)
The color picker opens upward as a floating panel: click outside, press Esc or click ✕ to close it
help.shortcutsText:
Ctrl + Z: undo (up to the last 10 steps; one drag or one burst of typing is one step); Ctrl + Y or Ctrl + Shift + Z: redo
Ctrl + S: save and stay in edit mode (use the Save button to save and leave)
Ctrl + C / X / V: copy / cut / paste the selected widgets (repeated pastes are staggered); Ctrl + D: duplicate in place
Ctrl + L: lock / unlock the selection; Ctrl + ] / [: one layer up / down, with Shift to the very top / bottom
Tab / Shift + Tab: select the next / previous widget; Esc: leave fullscreen, otherwise deselect
F11: fullscreen; F1: open this help (Ctrl is ⌘ on Mac)
While typing in an input box, Ctrl + Z / C / V keep their normal text meaning; only Ctrl + S still saves
help.variablesText:
The 'Variables' button in the toolbar: add / delete / rename (names appear in the widgets' data item dropdown and must be unique)
Control widgets such as buttons, switches and IO fields write to these variables; the definitions are saved and exported with the layout and are covered by undo
Deleting a variable that widgets are bound to asks for confirmation; those widgets are then unbound
help.displayText:
Saving leaves edit mode and the canvas fills the whole page
Right-click the page (long-press on touch screens): Edit / Refresh data sources / Export, Import layout
Export packs the layout and its images into one zip (Save As dialog); pick that zip to import (images are stored by the host under Resources/pic; images no longer referenced are cleaned up after saving)
help.controlText:
Buttons / switches / IO fields / sliders need a writable data source: currently only "Internal variables" is writable, product data is read-only
Buttons can also run the start / stop / clear / shaft collect commands

custom.htmlHint: Placed inside the body of an isolated iframe; inline script tags are allowed (the scada runtime is injected in head). Give the root element height: 100% to fill the widget.
custom.cssHint: Applies only to this widget's iframe. html / body are already 100% wide/high, no margin, transparent background; widget background / border / radius are set in the fields below.
custom.jsHint:
Runs as a normal script inside the iframe. Global object scada:
scada.onData(fn): called as fn(point, state) whenever data changes; point has value / text / name / unit / precision / standard / upper / lower / status / time, undefined when unbound
scada.point / scada.value / scada.history / scada.widget / scada.editing: current point / value / last 60 values / widget info (size, title, binding) / edit mode flag
scada.write(value): write back to the bound data source (must be writable, e.g. internal variables)
scada.format(v, digits) / scada.statusColor(status): number formatting / status colors
Script errors show at the widget's bottom-left in edit mode; right-click / long-press inside the iframe still opens the page menu

panel.imageTooLarge: Image exceeds {kb} KB, please compress it first
panel.transformPlaceholder:
e.g. return value * 1000
Leave empty to pass data through
panel.transformNoBinding: No data bound to this widget: value is null in the preview
panel.transformEmptyPreview: Type some code and the output will be previewed here with live data
panel.transformHint:
Args: value (current value), point (raw data point), ctx (history / state / widget).
Return: number → new value; string → display text; object → overrides value / text / unit / status / standard / upper / lower (status is re-evaluated when limits change); undefined → unchanged.
ctx.get(nameOrKey, source?): watch/read another data item (auto-subscribed; the function re-runs when it changes). ctx.setProp(key, value): temporarily override this widget's properties (any prop key plus hidden/x/y/w/h; not persisted); works in both edit and display mode, x/y/w/h apply in display mode only.
panel.title: Title
panel.titlePlaceholder: Leave empty to show the data item name
panel.scriptWhen:
Startup: runs once when entering display mode
Loop: runs repeatedly at the interval in both edit and display mode
Exit: runs before the app quits
panel.scriptHint:
Write plain JS statements (no wrapper function needed). Global object scada:
scada.read(nameOrKey, source?): read a data item (DataPoint, auto-subscribed)
scada.value(nameOrKey): numeric value (null when no data)
scada.write(nameOrKey, value): write to a writable source (e.g. internal variables)
scada.widgets(): all widgets (id / type / title)
scada.setProp(titleOrId, key, value): change widget properties at runtime (any prop key plus hidden/x/y/w/h; temporary override, not persisted)
scada.getProp(titleOrId, key): read a property (incl. runtime overrides)
scada.state: object shared by the three scripts; scada.log(...): console output
panel.noOptions: No data items in this source (check the product category config or tap "Refresh Sources")
panel.lockedHint: Locked: it cannot be moved, resized or deleted; unlock it to change position / size
panel.noneSelected: Tap a widget on the canvas to edit it; press Delete to remove the selected widget
